question.text: A satellite of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is orbiting the earth in a circular orbit at a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> above earth surface where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is the radius of the earth. If it starts losing energy at a constant rate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">β</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then it will fall on the earth surface after the time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>GMm</mi><mi>nβR</mi></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> Assuming that the satellite is approximately in a circular orbit at all times, find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
Ei=-GMm23R, Ef=-GMm2R

∴ βt=GMmR12–16

βt=GMm3R ⇒ t=GMm3βR
